Section 1 - Purpose
(1) QUT is committed to admission practices that accommodate student diversity and are based on the principles of transparency and equity. Admission to QUT award courses and non-award study is based on merit and perceived probability of academic success using procedures that are applied consistently and fairly with provisions made for underrepresented community groups.
Top of Page
Section 2 - Application
(2) This Policy relates to the admission of applicants to QUT award courses (Award Courses Policy) and non-award study (Non-award Study Policy) with the exception of Continuing Professional Education (CPE) course.
(3) This Policy does note relate to the admission of applicants to higher degree by research courses. The Higher Degree Research Candidates Policy outlines conditions for admissions to higher degree research courses.
Top of Page
Section 3 - Roles and Responsibilities
Position
Responsibility
University Academic Board
Approves the minimum entry requirements for each level of award course.
Faculty Academic Boards
Approves minimum entry requirements within approved limits for courses for which they have responsibility.
Vice-President (Administration) and University Registrar
Approves procedures for applying for admission to the University.
Determines the number of places available in each course for any admission period.
Determines the rank threshold for admission.
Makes all offers of admission.
Approves applications for deferment.
Approves admission schemes including adjustments, offer guarantees and eligibility/enriching schemes.
Specifies the minimum entry requirements for admissions schemes.
Approves the withdrawal or refusal of offers of admission.
Director, Student Administration
Manages the admission process, including the determination of qualification comparability.
Top of Page
Section 4 - Relationship to TEQSA Threshold Standards
(4) This Policy assists QUT to comply with the relevant requirements of the Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards) 2021. The primary standards supported by this Policy are:
1.1.1 - 1.1.3
7.2.1, 7.2.2d, 7.2.3
(5) This Policy also contributes to compliance with:
2.2.2
6.2.1h
7.2.2c
Top of Page
Section 5 - Application for Admission
(6) The admission application procedure differs for International applicants and domestic applicant and varies according to the course for which the application is made. Applicants must apply using the method and by the due date advised by the University.
Top of Page
Section 6 - Admission Requirements
(7) Applicants are assessed against the approved entry requirements for individual courses based on one or more of the following:
academic merit;
English language proficiency;
ability to satisfy any additional course entry requirements (e.g. portfolio, audition, interview, test, pre-requisite studies, nationality, location, employment);
minimum age.
Academic
(8) The Award Courses Policy and the Award Courses Procedure (QUT staff access only) specifies:
the general academic entry requirements applying to the different levels of award courses; and
the special provisions under which a Faculty Academic Board may specify additional course entry requirements.
(9) In determining academic merit, QUT may convert the applicant’s grades from other studies to QUT’s 7 point scale and calculate a grade point average to two decimal places so that a ranked order of merit can be determined.
(10) Minimum course entry requirements may assume knowledge of a subject area.
English Language Proficiency
(11) All candidates must meet the minimum English language proficiency requirement specified for each course. Unless otherwise specified, English proficiency may be demonstrated by an applicant through one or more of the following:
an IELTS academic test conducted no more than two years prior to the course start date (Note: QUT may determine equivalent scores on other approved English tests);
satisfactory completion of secondary schooling in Australia;
one year of successful full-time (or equivalent) accredited diploma level studies or higher in Australia;
successful completion of a recognised English bridging program;
successful completion of studies equivalent to secondary school or higher outside Australia where the medium of instruction is English and recognised by QUT.
Minimum Age
(12) QUT has a minimum age requirement for domestic and international students (with the exception of START QUT).
(13) Applicants under the age of 18 must have completed their secondary studies to year 12 level (or equivalent).
(14) QUT will not accept domestic applicant who would be under the age of 16 at the time that they commence their studies at the University.
(15) QUT will not accept international applicants who would be under the age of 17 at the time they commence their studies at the University. International applicants between the ages of 17 and 18 must demonstrate that they will reside with a parent, legal guardian or an approved person nominated by the parent or legal guardian; or that they have made other accommodation, support and welfare arrangements approved by the University.
Home Institution Approval
(16) In the case of cross-institutional applicants, admission is subject to home institution approval.
Top of Page
Section 7 - Adjustment Factors
(17) An adjustment factor can improve a Queensland Tertiary Admissions Centre (QTAC) applicant’s position in a ranked order of merit.
Equity adjustments are available to applicants who are recognised as having experienced educational disadvantage.
Elite sport adjustments are available to domestic applicant who are recognised elite sport students.
Subject adjustments are available to current school leavers who have completed recognised subjects during their senior secondary studies.
Top of Page
Section 8 - Indigenous Access Scheme
(18) QUT provides an admission selection process that considers prior learning and other personal achievements for Indigenous Australian applicants.
Top of Page
Section 9 - Recognition of Prior Learning
(19) To provide access to the broadest range of people possible, admission to QUT can be based on the Recognition of Prior Learning Framework (Recognition of Prior Learning Policy).
Top of Page
Section 10 - Offers of Admission
(20) Where demand exceeds the number of available places in a course, not all eligible applicants who satisfy the course entry requirements may be offered a place at QUT.
(21) Where an applicant meets a specified entry threshold, an offer of admission may be guaranteed into a course.
(22) An offer of admission may be conditional upon the applicant satisfying additional requirements specified by the Vice-President (Administration) and University Registrar in the offer.
(23) If a commencing student fails to enrol for the teaching period by the date specified in the University's offer of admission, or they have not fully satisfied all offer conditions by the date that the course commences, then the enrolment lapses and the offer of admission is withdrawn, unless an application to defer commencement of study has been submitted and approved.
(24) The Vice-President (Administration) and University Registrar may withdraw or refuse an offer of admission:
that was made for a future study period where the offered course or major has been approved for discontinuation prior to the commencement of that future study period;
that was made prior to changes in course entry requirements;
that was made because of the provision of incomplete or inaccurate information by the person, agent or a certifying authority;
that was made in error by QUT or its delegate (e.g. QTAC);
if they reasonably believe that, if enrolled, the person would pose an unacceptable risk to the safety or wellbeing of members of the QUT Community;
where the number of places in the offered course has filled.
Top of Page
Section 11 - Deferment
(25) QTAC applicants who have been offered admission may apply to defer commencement of their study for up to two years if the course has been approved for deferment.
(26) Deferred applicants will be subject to the course rules and fee structures in operation at the time of their new commencement.
(27) All other applicants seeking to defer commencement of their study should make application for a new offer of admission with a revised commencement date. The application will be assessed against the entry requirements that apply for the new commencement date.
Top of Page
Section 12 - Transfer of Course
(28) Domestic students who have studied and received grades in at least 48 credit points of study within a QUT undergraduate degree may apply for an internal transfer to a different degree at the same level, if the destination degree:
is covered by a QUT offer guarantee; and
carries no prerequisites, prior study, or additional entry requirements.
(29) Course transfer applicants must meet the published course entry threshold based on their QUT studies and approval is subject to availability of a place.
(30) The standard admission process can be used by students whose QUT studies do not qualify them for internal transfer; and/or for students who wish to change to a course not available through internal transfer.
Top of Page
Section 13 - International Applicants
(31) International applicants seeking an Australian student visa must satisfy QUT that they have a genuine intention to study at QUT will be assessed against the genuine student criteria in line with the Australian Government’s student visa regulations and the Migration Act 1958.
(32) QUT may offer a number of courses as a package of studies and include conditions to be satisfied before a student can progress from one course to the next. Students who need to delay the commencement of their second or a later course because they do not satisfy progression conditions should make application to defer their entry in line with Section 11 of this Policy, Deferment.
Top of Page
Section 14 - Single Unit Study
(33) In accordance with the Non-award Study Policy, applications may be made to QUT for admission to undertake single units of study without being admitted to an award course. Applicants for single unit study are responsible for obtaining information on unit availability, content, assumed knowledge and/or prerequisite requirements and timetables.
(34) A single unit study application for admission may be rejected if the applicant does not have an educational background (including English proficiency) appropriate to the unit/s applied for, or if there are insufficient places remaining in the class.
Top of Page
Section 15 - Return to Study
(35) Students who wish to re-enter a course after a period of absence and who are not returning from leave of absence, exclusion or deferment must reapply for admission. Generally, students returning to study will be considered for the current version of the course or, where appropriate, a replacement course and may be required to satisfy all course entry requirements, including any additional entry requirements, in operation at the time of their return and any new offer conditions.
(36) A student returning to study will not necessarily retain credit for all units completed prior to the absence. The length of the absence and changes to course content, external accreditation and structure during the intervening period will be considered when credits are determined. The Course Coordinator may require the student to repeat units that have been passed previously or to undertake additional units in order to satisfy the current course requirements.
(37) Students who wish to return to study a different course after a period of absence must apply for admission following the standard admission process for that course.
(38) Students who wish to return to study after a period of exclusion, suspension or refusal of enrolment under a QUT policy may not be eligible for direct re-admission and may be subject to specific conditions around their return imposed by the Vice-President (Administration) and University Registrar. These conditions will be communicated to students at the time of their exclusion or refusal of enrolment.
Top of Page
Section 16 - Suspension or Exclusion from a Tertiary Institution
(39) QUT will refuse admission to applicants who have been suspended from a post-secondary institution for non-academic reasons (discipline or misconduct) while the suspension or equivalent action remains in force.
(40) In accordance with QUT’s Academic Progress Policy, Readmission Following Exclusion, students who have been excluded from a course or study package at QUT or any other higher education institution as a result of unsatisfactory academic performance will not be considered for admission to a ‘like’ QUT course or study program unless:
at least 12 months have elapsed from the end of the teaching period for which the exclusion occurred; and the applicant has demonstrated rehabilitation and/or undertaken like study or professional work experience after their exclusion; or
the applicant is seeking to exit with a nested award course or a component course of a double degree, with no further study.
(41) The readmission of QUT students to the same course from which they have been excluded because of unsatisfactory academic performance is also subject to:
a place being available; and
the recommendation of the designated Executive Dean or Executive Director, QUT College who will make a recommendation to the Vice-President (Administration) and University Registrar as to whether the student should be readmitted.
(42) The provisions above do not apply if the applicant has been excluded from a ‘non-like’ course or study program.
(43) A QUT course or study program is regarded as ‘like’ if it is in the same discipline or study area or is similar to the course or study program from which the student has been excluded.
Top of Page
Section 17 - Appeals
(44) A student may seek review of any decision made under this Policy under the Review of Administrative Rulings Policy.
(45) If still dissatisfied after this review, applicants may appeal to the Appeals Committee of University Academic Board within five working days of the date of the notification of the outcome of the review.
Top of Page
Section 18 - Policy Specific Definitions
Term
Definitions
Non-award Study
For the purpose of this Policy, non-award study includes single unit study, bridging programs, enabling programs, foundation programs, English Language Intensive Courses for Overseas Students (ELICOS). It does not include Continuing Professional Education (CPE).
Home Institution
Is the institution where the student is undertaking their primary award course.
Top of Page
Section 19 - Obligations and Delegations
(46) QUT administers the admission process in accordance with the Higher Education Support Act 2003 (Cth) (HESA), the Education Services for Overseas Students Act 2000 (Cth) (ESOS) and the Migration Act 1958. Changes may be made to any provisions of these Acts at any time.
(47) QUT administers the admission process giving proper consideration to relevant human rights, in compliance with the Human Rights Act 2019.
(48) Refer to Register of Authorities and Delegations (C104, C105, C106) (QUT staff access only).
